_about: Seed for The Way. Loaded once into an empty database; after that the database is the record (./run.sh export-way writes it back out). Every duty here starts as a DRAFT until confirmed in the app. Row = [from_role, to_role, sphere, tradition, citation, text]. A row may carry a 7th element {status, reason, counter, attest: [[tradition, citation, quote], ...]}; 'reason' and 'counter' say why the house does not keep a retired duty and what commands stand against it. The top-level 'attest' list, [[row index, tradition, citation, quote], ...], records the same duty in more traditions. 'traditions' is listed in order of weight: Scripture first; 'Our house' (protocols drafted for the family, not received tradition) last, and judged against everything above it. 'role_fixes', [[row index, old from, old to, new from, new to], ...], corrects a duty's roles in a database that already holds it, unless the user has changed that duty's roles himself.

traditions.clan: Our house (lowest weight: judged against the rest)

roles.younger_sibling_in_law: Junior in-law of my generation (a brother-in-law younger than I; a younger brother's wife; my husband's younger sibling)
roles.entering: One being received into the family
roles.cut_off: One cut off from the family
roles.acting_head: Acting head (in place of one gone, or bound by kinship)
roles.in_keeping: One in the keeping of an acting head
roles.abandoned: One who has abandoned his family
roles.renounced: One who has stepped down from his headship
roles.co_parent: Other parent of one's child (never married)
roles.lineage_heir: Heir of the main line (종손 宗子)
roles.married_daughter: Married daughter (gone out to her husband's house)
roles.master: Master of the house (over servants and hired hands)
roles.servant: Servant or hired hand of the house

duties: Love her as Christ loved the church and gave himself for her.
Nourish and cherish her as his own body; provide for her.
Lead her as head for her good, and never be harsh or bitter with her.
Live with her with understanding and give her honor as a fellow heir of grace.
Keep faith with the wife of his youth: give her what is due and keep the marriage bed undefiled.
Lead her and the house in daily worship, prayer and the Word.
Rule with mildness; command rarely, reprove privately, and never strike.
Protect her, bear the heavier burdens, and provide for her if he should die first.
Submit to her own husband as to the Lord.
Respect him, in word and before others.
Keep faith with the husband of her youth: give him what is due and keep the marriage bed undefiled.
Be his helper; keep and build the home.
Guard his name and his secrets; do not shame him in company.
Total, exclusive and lifelong fidelity; the bond is not theirs to dissolve.
Be open to children and receive them as the crown of the marriage.
Help each other toward salvation: pray together, admonish gently, forgive quickly.
Dwell together; do not live apart without necessity.
Keep the distinction of husband and wife: each holds their own office and does not usurp the other's.
Covenant Home: Parental Honoring Protocol I.3
No secret money: nothing is sent to either family without both knowing.
Bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord; teach them daily.
Discipline them while there is hope.
Do not provoke them to anger or discourage them.
Provide for them and lay up an inheritance.
Gouge, Of Domestical Duties (1622), Treatise 6; Gen 24
See them well married: seek out, counsel and approve a worthy spouse in good time.
Train each child to a calling by which they can live.
Be their first teachers in faith and virtue; this cannot be handed to others.
Keep affection between father and child; do not let rank freeze it.
Love, pray for and bless them; instruct, counsel and admonish them.
Covenant Home: Parental Honoring Protocol II
Once they marry, counsel when asked and let the new house govern itself.
Honor father and mother all their days.
Obey them in the Lord while under their roof; weigh their counsel after.
Repay them: support them in age and need, and do not excuse it away.
Do not despise or abandon them when they are old.
Reverence in heart, word and behavior; bear with their infirmities and cover them in love.
No contempt, mockery or rebellion that shames them.
Grown children owe material and moral support in old age, illness and loneliness.
Serve them with reverence; feeding them alone is no more than is done for animals.
When they are wrong, remonstrate gently, and remain respectful if not heeded.
Do not go far away without letting them know where you are.
Come home or call at Seollal and Chuseok and on their birthdays.
Covenant Home: Parental Honoring Protocol II.2-3
Ask their advice before major decisions; if choosing otherwise, explain it to them with honor.
Covenant Home: Parental Honoring Protocol I.2
Send the regular gift to parents, agreed between husband and wife.
Marry with your parents' knowledge and blessing sought, not behind their backs.
Carry first responsibility for parents in age and for gathering the house.
Keep the family's remembrances and records and hand them on.
Mencius 3A:4 (長幼有序); 兄友弟恭
Be kind to younger siblings, set the example and look after them.
Mencius 3A:4 (長幼有序); 兄友弟恭
Show respect to elder siblings and give them precedence.
Stand with a brother in adversity; dwell in unity.
Be your brother's keeper: no hatred, and no shutting the hand against his need.
Share the care of parents; do not leave it to one.
Tell the coming generation what God has done; teach your children's children.
Leave an inheritance to your children's children.
Rise before the gray head; be their crown.
Share in repaying them with care.
Covenant Home: Parental Honoring Protocol III.3
Give your parents real time with their grandchildren, in person or by call.
Receive a child's spouse as your own child; bless and counsel them.
Let them leave and cleave: do not rule or divide the new house.
Honor a spouse's parents as your own.
Share in the care of her husband's parents.
Be a son to his wife's parents, not a guest: help and visit.
Treat a spouse's siblings and siblings' spouses as brothers and sisters.
Stand in for the parents where they fail or die; come to the rescue of a brother's child.
Honor uncles and aunts as elders.
Honor one another and rejoice in each other's advancement as your own.
Commend those who do well and reprove those who do ill; protect and provide for them.
By grave, wise, holy example keep the authority God has given.
Do not command what is unlawful, correct unduly, provoke to wrath, or leave them exposed to wrong and temptation.
Reverence, prayer and thanksgiving for them; willing heed to lawful counsel; defense of their person and name.
Give honor first; no envy at another's gifts and no grasping for pre-eminence.
Treat older men as fathers and older women as mothers.
Do not hide from your own flesh: help a kinsman in real need.
Be reconciled quickly: go to him first, in private.
Cover a kinsman's fault; do not carry it outside the family.
Rejoice at their weddings and births; mourn at their funerals.
The family owes care to its young, old, sick and poor members.
Command his house after him to keep the way of the Lord.
Hold family worship and see the Lord's Day kept by all under his roof.
Rule his own house well, with all dignity.
Provide for his own; whoever will not has denied the faith.
Covenant Home: Parental Honoring Protocol III.2
Stand in front: take criticism aimed at his wife or children upon himself.
Keep the home a domestic church.
Hear and settle disputes between kin before they harden.
Bless the houses and their children by name.
Keep the record of the family and gather it at the appointed times.
See that no young man or woman of the family is left without help toward marriage.
Guard the family's good name in how you live.
Attend the weddings, funerals and great birthdays of the family, or send word and a gift.
Covenant Home: Tradition and Culture II
On the anniversaries of our dead, tell their stories (remembrance, not jesa).
Stay reachable: answer the family, and do not go silent for seasons.
Loyalty: take the family's side in public and bring grievances to the family in private.
Do not count him an enemy; warn him as a brother.
Keep the door open: receive him back gladly when he turns.
Do not carry on as though nothing has happened while he holds to the offense.
Keep praying for him by name.
Come back: own the wrong plainly and seek to be restored.
Go after the one who has drifted: make the first move, and keep making it.
Do not isolate yourself: answer, show up, and say what the grievance is.
Welcome the one coming in: learn their name, their people and their story.
Teach the newcomer the ways of the house plainly and patiently.
Take this people as your own: learn its ways and honor its elders.
Delight in her alone; let her love satisfy him always.
Give her time and gladness: enjoy life with the wife he loves.
Pray with her and for her; harshness toward her hinders his prayers.
Uphold her authority in the house: let the children and household honor her as mistress under him.
Speak well of her, and never disgrace her before the children or others.
Treat her with the courtesy due a guest, never with the contempt of familiarity.
Keep dignity and respect between husband and wife even in private; the order of the house begins there.
Do him good and not harm all the days of her life; let his heart safely trust her.
Win him by pure and reverent conduct where words do not.
Gouge, Of Domestical Duties (1622), Treatise 3; Acts 5:29
Yield to his lawful direction cheerfully, not grudgingly; where conscience forbids, refuse meekly.
Be careful with the household's goods: neither waste them nor give them away without his consent.
Hold the place of the heart as he holds the place of the head: the order of love, not servitude.
Support his work and his name from within the house.
Make her husband's house her own: his parents and kin are now hers to honor.
Guard the bond: what God has joined, no one separates.
Do not let the sun go down on anger; forgive as God forgave you.
Do not seek a divorce: only adultery, or willful desertion that cannot be remedied, can loose the bond.
Receive children as a heritage from the Lord.
Praise each other at home and before others.
Train each child in the way he should go.
Pity them and give good gifts, as the Father does.
Teach them to marry only in the Lord.
Train them with tenderness, affection and patience; it is dangerous to make children afraid of you.
Train them to a habit of obedience, and to always speaking the truth.
Train them to a knowledge of the Bible and a habit of prayer.
Train them by the example of your own life; they will not believe you are in earnest otherwise.
Make a home where tenderness, forgiveness, respect, fidelity and disinterested service are the rule.
When they are grown, advise them in their choice of calling and spouse; do not force them.
Be a father in fact, so that the son can be a son.
Do not let correction destroy affection: where anger rises, let another good man teach him.
Teach manners at the table: precedence to elders, honorific speech, and thanks.
Mark the hundredth day and the first birthday with the family gathered and the child blessed.
Rise early and intercede for each child by name.
Bless each child by name before he dies.
Set his house in order: make his will and name his heirs, so the house is not left to quarrel.
Watch for a child who has gone astray, and run to meet him when he turns.
Teach them the faith from infancy, with wisdom and kindness on her tongue.
Love her children; be the steady warmth of the home.
Choose the child's surroundings with care, as Mencius' mother moved house three times.
Never curse, mock or scorn them.
See that a widowed mother is cared for, as Christ did from the cross.
Bring them near in their old age and provide for them, as Joseph did.
Bury them with honor, and do not neglect the surviving parent.
Respect them with gratitude for the gift of life and for their love and work.
Obey while living at home; when grown, obedience ends but respect does not.
Know your parents' ages: rejoice at their long life and fear for their frailty.
Keep a willing and cheerful face in serving them; the countenance is the hard part.
Serve them by the proper forms while they live; bury and remember them by the proper forms when they die.
Xiaojing 1 (身體髮膚 受之父母)
Do not harm your body; you received it from them.
Xiaojing 1 (立身揚名 以顯父母)
Establish yourself and make a good name, so that it honors them.
Care for their wishes, not only their bodies.
Ask after them regularly, as the old way did evening and morning.
Speak to them in honorific speech; give and receive with both hands.
Gather the family for their sixtieth, seventieth and eightieth birthdays.
Make the New Year's bow and receive their words of blessing.
Hold memorial worship on the anniversary of a parent's death.
Recompense them: relieve them in want and bear with them in weakness, as they bore with you.
Stay close to her own parents without neglecting her husband's.
Do not pass over the firstborn's right out of favoritism.
Prepare the eldest son to carry the house: teach him its affairs, its people and its record.
Forgive and provide for your brothers, as Joseph did.
If a brother falls poor and sells his land, redeem it.
Keep harmony with brothers and sisters: respect, gratitude and help.
Share fairly the cost and work of the parents' occasions.
Help younger siblings through school and toward marriage when the parents cannot.
Be a good younger brother or sister: yield and follow; it is the root of humaneness.
Bless and counsel them, and never undercut their parents' authority.
Hold them, know them, and be glad in them.
Visit, call and greet them; ask for their stories.
Never set your child against their spouse; speak well of the spouse to your child.
Weigh a parent-in-law's counsel seriously, as Moses heeded Jethro.
Greet and serve her husband's parents with the honor due her own.
Prepare the holidays and family occasions with her mother-in-law.
Treat the other house with formal courtesy and speak no ill of it.
Meet at the great occasions and keep the bond between the two houses.
Be a second father or mother: take an interest in their schooling, faith and marriage.
Care for an aged uncle or aunt who has no children to do it.
Help a cousin in real need: an uncle's son is among the near kin who may redeem.
Keep the cousins close: they are the next generation of the clan.
Provide for a stepchild as for your own household.
Rule with a parent's tenderness, winning trust before asking much.
Honor a step-parent as one set over you in a parent's place.
Love, pray for and bless those under you.
Let the elder go first in seating, speaking and serving.
Wait for the eldest to begin eating; rise when an elder enters.
Know the state of the household's affairs and look after them.
Keep order: set times for work, worship, meals and rest.
Lead family worship daily: Scripture, prayer and singing.
Order the house by first ordering himself.
As head of the house, answer for it before the clan and the world.
Keep a will and a plan, so the house is not left in confusion.
Accept the order of the house set by its head.
Do your share of the work of the house.
Do not bring trouble on your own house.
Liji, Dazhuan (尊祖敬宗 收族)
Gather the kin: know them, help them, and keep them together.
Call the family together at least yearly and hear each house.
Lead willingly, not domineering, but by example.
Hand the faith and the story of the family to the next generation.
Honor the forefathers, and so revere the head of the family.
Bring disputes with kin to the Head of the family before outsiders.
Contribute to the common needs of the family.
Report births, marriages and deaths for the family record.
Pray for the dead of the family.
Introduce the newcomer to the elders in person.
Pray for them by name, and keep track of how they are.
Speak no evil of the family to outsiders.
Redeem and relieve: stand as the near kinsman for their needs, their land and their debts.
Keep the name of the dead alive in his house; do not let it be cut off.
Seek a worthy marriage for the widows and the unmarried in his keeping.
Do not rule over them harshly; he holds the place in trust, not as owner.
Visit the fatherless and the widow in their affliction; be a father to the fatherless.
Pray for them, and bring them under the Word with his own house.
Help without shaming them, as Boaz let Ruth glean among the sheaves.
Give the house back when a man of its own line returns or comes of age.
As one in a father's place: protect, counsel and provide for them in all things needful for soul and body.
Where their own family cannot provide, take on its care: the old, the sick and the poor.
Take in those whose house has failed, as the lineage head gathers the kin.
Stand for them at weddings, funerals and in dealings with other houses, as their own head would.
Receive his care with gratitude and heed his counsel.
Give him the honor due one in a father's place: willing heed to his lawful counsel, and fidelity.
Do not live idly on his help: work, and bear what you can.
Keep him truly informed of your needs and doings; hide nothing he must answer for.
Call him back plainly to the house he left; warn him as a brother, not an enemy.
Keep his place for him to return to, while another acts in it.
Turn back: let the father's heart turn to his children.
Provide for his own still, even while away.
Honor him still for what he was and is, though he no longer leads.
Never speak against the other parent before the children.
Pay what is owed for the children, and keep your word even when it costs.
Remain open to reconciliation: before God the bond may still stand.
Work together for the child's good, and speak no ill of each other before him.
Do not treat him as a husband or a son-in-law; say plainly the union is not a marriage, and call it to marriage or to an end.
A free union is not a marriage; do not bless it as one.
Be courteous and truthful with him; he is a neighbor, not an enemy.
Show hospitality to those not of the family.
Bury the dead with care and decency, at the family's cost if need be.
Mourn them openly, but not as those who have no hope.
Carry out a dead father's or mother's just wishes and settled commands.
Keep their good name: speak truly of them, and let their memory be a blessing.
Mark and keep their grave, and lay the family's dead with their fathers where they can be found.
Show kindness to those they left behind, for the dead one's sake.
Tell their story and God's dealings with them to the children, and imitate their faith.
Give thanks to God for them, not to them.
Do not call on the dead, pray to them, or seek their counsel or blessing.
Do not set food or drink before the dead, or bow to their tablet, portrait or body as part of a rite.
Directory for the Publick Worship of God (1645), Concerning Burial of the Dead
Give the dead every civil respect due their station at burial, without ceremonies toward the body that cannot benefit the dead.
At a funeral, bow to the mourners and comfort them; stand in silence before the dead rather than bow to them.
Honor and serve the parents who adopted or raised you as your own father and mother all their lives, without forsaking the parents who bore you.

Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, 양자 養子 … 연원 및 변천

duties: Mourn your adoptive parents as a natural child mourns his own.

『경국대전(經國大典)』에 수양자는 양부와 양모상을 당해서 재최(齊衰) 삼년상을 치루도록 명시되어 있다 — Gyeongguk daejeon requires a three-year mourning for adoptive parents.

duties: Raise an adopted child as fully your own, with no difference from a child of your body, in love and in inheritance.

attest: 惟當撫之如子，以其財產與之 — Treat him as a son and give him your property.

duties: Marry and raise children, so that the family line is carried on.
